Fixes: #7349

This is currently throwing a null error when the instruction is not
recognized by the router, and AFAICT there is no way to catch that.

body: Thanks @petebacondarwin ; is there any way at all to catch the current error? I was not able to find one, which means that this exception always escapes and, in our case, crashes the entire app. Unless a way exists to handle router errors in general, I think throwing a better error would not solve the issue in a meaningful way. Also, I would personally consider this at least a P1 issue, again under the assumption that there is currently no way of catching router errors. If such a way exists, then P2 is appropriate.

What I am suggesting is that for the time being, it would probably be better to just avoid throwing errors entirely (which is what I propose in #7203 ), rather than throwing unrecoverable ones. When a better mechanism exists for handling them, then a more meaningful error may be thrown instead.
I think I have a fix almost ready.
